children: By Pawel Florkiewicz and Alan Charlish

The National Bank of Poland kept its main interest rate at 3.75% on Wednesday, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.

The decision by the Monetary Policy Council is in line with economists' expectations. All 29 respondents in a Reuters poll forecast that the NBP would keep its main interest rate (PLNINT=ECI) at 3.75% in September.
Inflation rose to 3.4% on the year in August, more than expected by analysts and nearing the top end of the central bank's target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.

"This was mainly due to the rise in the annual growth in prices of fuels for personal transport equipment. It can be estimated that in August inflation net of food and energy prices also increased," the central bank said in a statement.
"Against this background the Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged."
The NBP said that further decisions by the Council would depend on incoming information regarding the outlook for inflation and economic activity in Poland.
"Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context," it said.
The MPC reiterated that fiscal policy, changes in the dynamics of economic activity in Poland, and the future path of wage dynamics also remain risk factors for the inflation outlook.
A draft budget for 2027 projected that the general government deficit-to-GDP ratio will remain unchanged next year at 7.1% and will ease only marginally from 7.3% in 2025.
Governor Adam Glapinski said in July he could propose a 25-basis-point interest rate cut after the summer.

"Although Governor Glapinski had previously suggested the possibility of filing a motion for a rate cut after the summer holidays, the recent rise in global uncertainty and the spike in CPI inflation have made such a move impossible," said PKO Bank on X.
According to PKO analysts, interest rates will remain unchanged through the end of the year, with the time for cuts potentially arriving in mid-2027.
The market is now waiting for Thursday's press conference with the NBP governor, who will justify the central bank's decisions. The bank last cut interest rates in March.
